description: Canonical pytest corpus for CI (SECP test-pipeline acceleration). The complete required backend test corpus, divided into balanced parallel shards. Every Git-tracked pytest-discoverable file under `roots` is assigned to exactly one shard; a new managed test file is auto-included, and a new pytest-shaped file outside `roots` fails the inventory closed unless it is listed in `exclusions`.

exclusions.reason: Runtime worker preflight-wiring self-test MODULE (SECP-B2-4.2), not a pytest suite. It matches the `*_test.py` glob but lives in the `secp_worker` source package (not a test root), contains no `test_*` functions or `Test*` classes, performs no I/O, and is imported as a normal module by apps/api/tests/test_readonly_preflight_activation.py (which exercises it as a unit under test). Collecting it as tests would collect zero nodes and misrepresent it as a suite.

The PostgreSQL + real-socket read-after-write gate. It is pytest-shaped and lives OUTSIDE the canonical roots on purpose, and is run instead by the dedicated `backend-api-socket-gate` CI job (machine-checked in tests/test_ci_workflow.py, which also proves this exclusion exists — so it can never become 'excluded and run by nothing'). Two reasons it is not in the shards. (1) It carries `xfail(strict=True, raises=ReadAfterWriteViolation)` while the `Depends(db_session, scope="function")` fix is pending, and pytest records an xfail in JUnit as `<skipped type="pytest.xfail">`. The shard skip accounting classifies skips by REASON, so this one would be accepted only because the words 'PostgreSQL' happen to appear in the marker text — an accidental green in the one place this repo most insists on deliberate ones. (2) It binds a real TCP listener and serves uvicorn for the duration of a test; that belongs in a dedicated job, not four-way-parallel inside the required corpus. Nothing here weakens the corpus: no existing module is removed, and this file has never been in it.

The PostgreSQL + real-socket gate for the Proxmox operator command surface (SECP-P7-A). Pytest-shaped and OUTSIDE the canonical roots on purpose, run instead by the dedicated `backend-operator-surface-socket-gate` CI job (machine-checked in tests/test_ci_workflow.py, which also proves this exclusion exists, so it can never become 'excluded and run by nothing'). Two reasons it is not in the shards, and neither is the read-after-write gate's xfail reason — this module carries no expected-failure marker and its job requires every test to pass outright. (1) It binds a real TCP listener and serves uvicorn for the duration of the module; that belongs in a dedicated job rather than four-way-parallel inside the required corpus, where a port-exhausted runner would go red for every stream. (2) It is the ONLY place four properties are proven over the wire rather than by direct function call — every command route refuses an unauthenticated caller, organization scoping holds, target scoping holds, and an ordinary (enrolled-but-not-healthy) worker cannot be used for controlled-live execution — and its job's exact-count accounting is calibrated to that module alone. It contacts no Proxmox cluster, runs no OpenTofu, starts no container and spawns no process; the only listener is an ephemeral loopback port inside the runner. Nothing here weakens the corpus: no existing module is removed, and the unit-level proofs of the same surface remain in apps/api/tests/test_proxmox_operator_commands.py inside the shards.

Runtime worker readiness SELF-TEST seam (SECP-002B-1B B1B-PR4), not a pytest suite. It matches the `*_test.py` glob but lives in the `secp_worker` source package (not a test root), contains no `test_*` functions or `Test*` classes, performs no I/O (the shipped default is `SealedPlanSecretSelfTest`, which contacts nothing), and is imported as a normal module by the readiness orchestration and by apps/api/tests/test_readiness_*.py (which exercise it as a unit under test). Collecting it as tests would collect zero nodes and misrepresent it as a suite.

notes: roots is the authoritative corpus. It intentionally ADDS contracts/scenario-schema/tests, which the pre-acceleration workflow (`pytest apps/api/tests tests`) omitted — a coverage correction, not a scope expansion.
No pytest suites exist under apps/worker, contracts/plugin-api, plugins, or other packages (verified against the Git-tracked file inventory).

The PR5F fixed-layout root transaction module lives under the canonical `tests` root. Its dedicated Linux-root no-skip job is additive; normal shards still collect it and observe its explicit non-root skip.
Sharding is by FILE: every node in a file runs in the same shard, so the node-level union of shards equals the canonical collection with empty pairwise intersection.
PostgreSQL-gated, migration, immutability, concurrency, boundary, schema, and security tests are all inside roots and are never excluded; each shard runs against its own real PostgreSQL service.

apps/acceptance/tests holds the HERMETIC contract tests of the two-host acceptance harness (evidence schema, closed vocabularies, argv contracts, reason-code provenance). They import no Docker and create no host, so they belong in the ordinary shards. The harness's own end-to-end run is a separate, manually dispatched workflow — it needs privileged nested containers and is not part of the required gate.
